title: PLL Building Blocks
intro: A design-oriented companion to the Phase-Locked Loops and Oscillators chapters: the circuits that make up a charge-pump PLL, phase-frequency detector, charge pump, loop filter and VCO, compared in enough depth to choose between them for a real design.

blocks.alt: Phase-frequency detector made of two reset flip-flops and an AND gate, driving a charge pump of two switched current sources and an RC loop filter whose output is the VCO control voltage.
blocks.caption: The blocks this chapter compares: PFD, charge pump and loop filter (the VCO follows).

blocks.text: Each block owns part of the specification. The PFD and charge pump set the in-band noise floor, the static phase offset and most of the reference spur; the loop filter sets bandwidth, phase margin and spur rejection; the VCO sets the out-of-band noise, the tuning range and, through its noise, how wide the loop has to be. The divider multiplies every in-band contribution by $N^2$. Because the blocks interact, a choice made for one (a ring VCO, say) constrains the others (a high reference frequency and a wide, well-damped loop).

items: In-band phase noise: PFD/CP floor $+\ 10\log_{10}f_{PFD} + 20\log_{10}N$, plus reference and divider noise.
Out-of-band phase noise: the VCO, high-pass shaped by the loop.
Integrated jitter: both, with the loop bandwidth chosen near where they cross.
Reference spurs: charge-pump mismatch, switching errors and leakage, divided by the filter's attenuation at $f_{ref}$, times $K_{VCO}$.
Lock range and tuning: the VCO's bands and calibration, plus the charge pump's output compliance.
Area and power: dominated by the loop-filter capacitors and the LC VCO's inductor, or by the ring VCO's power for a given jitter.
Phase-Frequency Detector Circuits: what a PFD must do, flip-flop, TSPC and precharged PFDs, the reset path, blind zone and maximum frequency, driving the pump, how to choose.
Dead Zone, Reset Pulses and PFD Linearity: the dead zone in numbers, choosing the reset pulse, static phase offset from mismatch, linearity for fractional-N (interactive PFD characteristic).
Other Phase Detectors: Bang-Bang, Sampling and TDCs: bang-bang and Hogge detectors, sampling and sub-sampling detectors, time-to-digital converters, and a comparison.
In-Band Noise: The PFD and Charge-Pump Floor: where in-band noise comes from, charge-pump noise against current, normalised floor and flicker figures, the jitter-power FoM (interactive noise budget).
Charge-Pump Topologies: switches at drain, source or gate, current steering, differential and active-filter pumps, and how to choose.
Charge-Pump Mismatch, Leakage and Reference Spurs: error sources, mismatch against output voltage, estimating the reference spur, remedies.
Charge-Pump Circuit Design: choosing the pump current, active current matching, a sizing procedure and a worked design.
Loop Filter Design: closed-form second-order filter design, phase margin from the capacitor ratio, choosing bandwidth, third-order and active filters (interactive phase margin).
Oscillator Phase Noise and Figures of Merit: Leeson's model, the impulse sensitivity function, FoM and its limits, phase noise to jitter (interactive ring against LC).
LC VCO Topologies Compared: current- and voltage-limited regimes, NMOS-only, complementary, tail-filtered, class-C, class-D, class-F and Colpitts cores, the tank.
Ring VCO Topologies and When They Are Enough: starved, supply-controlled and symmetric-load rings, ring phase noise and supply sensitivity, injection locking and MDLLs.
VCO Tuning Range, Band Switching and Calibration: capacitor banks, K_VCO across bands, varactor linearity, automatic frequency calibration, pushing and pulling.
Choosing a VCO: from specification to required FoM, family and core, with three worked cases.
Selecting a PLL Architecture: the candidate architectures side by side, a decision procedure, what to simulate, and common mistakes.

blocks.text: If you are choosing a design, start with Selecting a PLL Architecture, then use Choosing a VCO and the In-Band Noise widget to check the numbers for your specification, and the circuit pages to pick each block's topology.

The Phase-Locked Loops chapter (charge-pump PLLs, type II loop dynamics, jitter transfer) and the Oscillators chapter (LC tanks, cross-coupled oscillators, varactors, the VCO model). Noise and Mismatch chapters help with the charge-pump pages.

blocks.title: Where does the noise come from?
blocks.text: A PLL's measured phase noise is flat at $-105$ dBc/Hz up to 500 kHz and falls at 20 dB per decade beyond 2 MHz. Which blocks set each part, and what would you change to lower each?
solution: The flat in-band part is the PFD/CP (and reference, divider) floor times $N^2$: raise $I_P$, shorten the reset pulse, raise $f_{ref}$ to reduce $N$, or use a lower-noise detector.
The 20 dB per decade part beyond the loop bandwidth is the VCO: a better FoM (more power, better tank, better core) lowers it. Widening the loop pushes the VCO region out but extends the flat floor.
blocks.answer: In-band: detector and pump; out-of-band: the VCO.

items: B. Razavi, Design of Analog CMOS Integrated Circuits, 2nd ed., McGraw-Hill, 2017, Chapters 15 and 16.
B. Razavi, Design of CMOS Phase-Locked Loops: From Circuit Level to Architecture Level, Cambridge University Press, 2020.
